question: What did Katie Hobbs do for the state of Arizona in the last 12 months?
subject: ballot-az-pima:governor|Katie Hobbs
visibleText:
Katie Hobbs · Governor

From what we have on record, Katie Hobbs — the sitting Governor — signed six executive orders in the past 12 months: "Protecting Arizonans' Healthcare Freedom" (Sept. 11, 2025), "Removing Barriers to Delivering Affordable Energy for Arizona" (Sept. 15, 2025), one granting the Arizona Department of Homeland Security authority to receive criminal history record information (Nov. 5, 2025), "Cutting Taxes for Hard-Working Arizonans" (Nov. 25, 2025), "Protecting Paychecks for Hard-Working Arizonans" (May 20, 2026), and one barring state workers from using nonpublic information for personal profit (July 8, 2026). Her office's own site also references a 2026 State of the State address, erasing about $1 billion in medical debt, a memorandum of understanding with the Navajo Nation on economic development, and a statement on the Colorado River. Two limits on our end: these are executive orders only — we have not recorded bills she signed or vetoed, because the legislature's bill-status system can't be read automatically — and we read 12 of the 37 executive orders we indexed, so the list above may not be complete. She has also filed as a Democrat for Governor in the November 3, 2026 general election.

These are executive orders only. We have not recorded bills signed or vetoed — the legislature's bill-status system does not permit automated reading, so that half of the record is not ours to show yet.

We read 12 of the 37 executive orders we indexed, and the index continues past what we walked.

visibleText:

Proposition 423: Vail Unified School District budget override continuation

Proposition 423 asks voters in Vail Unified School District No. 20 whether the district may continue to exceed its revenue control limit by no more than 12.5% per fiscal year, for 2027/2028 and the following six fiscal years. It's a continuation of an existing budget override, not a new one. According to the district's Notice of Election, that would put the budget about $5,102,762 above the alternate budget in 2027/2028, at an estimated $1.61 per $100 of secondary assessed valuation. The district board adopted the resolution calling the election on June 2, 2026, and it appears as a special election consolidated with the November 3, 2026 General Election. You vote yes or no.

Proposition 423 asks voters in Vail Unified School District No. 20 whether the district may continue exceeding its revenue control limit — its state-set budget cap — by up to 12.5% per year, starting with fiscal year 2027/2028 and for the six fiscal years after that. According to the district's Notice of Election, that would put the budget roughly $5,102,762 above the alternate (non-override) budget for 2027/2028, at an estimated continued cost of $1.61 per $100 of secondary assessed valuation.
